column1: # Columns, separated by a TAB:  context <TAB> English source text <TAB> translation
#   context  usually empty. `@plural`, `@id` and `@msg` mean something to the app; any other
#            word is a label that tells apart two meanings of the same English (`event` marks
#            the phrases replaced inside the simulator's event summaries).
#   escapes  \n  \t  \\  inside a column. `{}` placeholders (messages with parts) must appear
#            the same number of times in both columns, in the order the language wants, and a
#            trailing "…" in one needs one in the other.
#   @plural  English `one|other`; the translation lists this language's plural forms, `|`-separated.
#   Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored. A missing entry shows in English.
# Clean room: every entry was written from the plain meaning of the English text in ordinary
# computing vocabulary. No other product's localisation, string table or translated UI was
# consulted or copied; add entries the same way.

column2: S1 creates VLANs 10 and 20; the clients S2 and S3 learn them (`show vtp status`, `show vlan brief`). Add `vlan 30` on S1 and look again on a client. PC1 reaches PC3 (VLAN 10), PC2 reaches PC4 (VLAN 20).

column2: PC1 and PC2 autoconfigure from R1's router advertisements (ipv6config). Try `ping 2001:db8:2::10` from PC1, `show ipv6 route` and `show ipv6 neighbors` on the routers, and watch NDP in Simulation mode.
column3: PC1 y PC2 se autoconfiguran con los anuncios de router de R1 (ipv6config). Prueba `ping 2001:db8:2::10` desde PC1, `show ipv6 route` y `show ipv6 neighbors` en los routers, y observa NDP en el modo Simulación.

column2: MLS1 routes between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 (`ip routing`, interfaces Vlan10 and Vlan20) and sends everything else to R1 over a routed port (`no switchport`). Try `show ip route` on MLS1 and a ping from PC1 to PC4 or to SRV1.
column3: MLS1 enruta entre la VLAN 10 y la VLAN 20 (`ip routing`, interfaces Vlan10 y Vlan20) y manda todo lo demás a R1 por un puerto enrutado (`no switchport`). Prueba `show ip route` en MLS1 y un ping de PC1 a PC4 o a SRV1.

column2: Every router runs RIPv2. Compare `show ip route` (R routes, hop counts in `show ip rip database`) on R1 and R3, then shut R2's g0/1 and watch the routes go.
column3: Todos los routers ejecutan RIPv2. Compara `show ip route` (rutas R; los saltos en `show ip rip database`) en R1 y R3, luego apaga g0/1 de R2 y verás desaparecer las rutas.

column2: The red cable is serial; the clock marks R1's DCE end (`show controllers s0/0/0`). Remove the clock rate on R1, or change one end to `encapsulation hdlc`, and the link goes down.
column3: El cable rojo es serie; el reloj marca el extremo DCE de R1 (`show controllers s0/0/0`). Quita el clock rate en R1, o cambia un extremo a `encapsulation hdlc`, y el enlace se cae.

column2: R1 is active for both virtual gateways (`show standby`). Watch the HSRP hellos in Simulation mode, then shut R1's interfaces and ping from PC1 again.

column2: PC1 pings the Web server through PAT (`show ip nat translations` on Office). PC2 is blocked by the GUESTS access list (`show access-lists`). The ISP has no route to 192.168.0.0/24: only NAT makes the replies come back.

column2: PCs get their addresses from R1 by DHCP (Desktop > IP Configuration > DHCP, or `ipconfig /renew`). R1's console asks for `cisco`; `enable` asks for `class`. Try `show ip dhcp binding` on R1.
column3: Los PC reciben su dirección de R1 por DHCP (Desktop > IP Configuration > DHCP, o `ipconfig /renew`). La consola de R1 pide `cisco`; `enable` pide `class`. Prueba `show ip dhcp binding` en R1.

column2:
R1 joins two LANs.

1. Name the router R1.
2. Protect privileged mode with the secret class.
3. Give GigabitEthernet0/0 the address 192.168.10.1/24 and GigabitEthernet0/1 192.168.20.1/24, and turn both on.
4. Check that PC1 reaches PC2.

Press Check Results at any time.
column3:
R1 une dos LAN.

1. Llama R1 al router.
2. Protege el modo privilegiado con la contraseña secret class.
3. Da a GigabitEthernet0/0 la dirección 192.168.10.1/24 y a GigabitEthernet0/1 la 192.168.20.1/24, y actívalas.
4. Comprueba que PC1 llega a PC2.

Pulsa Comprobar resultados cuando quieras.

column2: WLC1 holds two WLANs (`show wlan`, `show capwap`): Staff checks logins with RADIUS1 (users ana/ana12345 and luis/luis1234) and lands in VLAN 10 (192.168.10.0/24); Guest uses the passphrase invitado123 and lands in VLAN 30 (192.168.30.0/24). The access points tag each WLAN on their trunk to S1, and R1 routes and hands out addresses per VLAN. In Simulation mode, reset and ping from Laptop1 to watch the 802.11 association, the EAP login, the RADIUS exchange, the 4-way handshake and then CCMP-protected data; move Laptop1 next to LAP2 and watch it reassociate, keeping its address.
column3: WLC1 tiene dos WLAN (`show wlan`, `show capwap`): Staff comprueba los inicios de sesión con RADIUS1 (usuarios ana/ana12345 y luis/luis1234) y entra en la VLAN 10 (192.168.10.0/24); Guest usa la frase de paso invitado123 y entra en la VLAN 30 (192.168.30.0/24). Los puntos de acceso etiquetan cada WLAN en su troncal hacia S1, y R1 enruta y reparte direcciones en cada VLAN. En modo Simulación, reinicia y haz ping desde Laptop1 para ver la asociación 802.11, el inicio de sesión EAP, el intercambio RADIUS, el saludo de 4 vías y después los datos protegidos con CCMP; acerca Laptop1 a LAP2 y verás cómo se reasocia sin perder su dirección.

column2: FW1 lets the office out (sharing its outside address), keeps the Internet out of the office, and publishes the DMZ web server through a fixed address and one access rule.
column3: FW1 deja salir a la oficina (compartiendo su dirección externa), impide que Internet entre en la oficina y publica el servidor web de la DMZ con una dirección fija y una regla de acceso.

column2: FW1 has three named interfaces: inside (level 100), dmz (50) and outside (0). The office and the DMZ reach the Internet through the outside address (`show xlate`, `show conn`); Home can't start anything towards them, except the web server, published as 203.0.113.10 by a static rule and one access rule (`show access-list` counts the hits). From Home, browse http://203.0.113.10 and ping PC1 to see the difference; `show logging` on FW1 tells why a packet was dropped. The global policy inspects ICMP, so pings from the office come back without a rule; FW1 is not a hop, so a traceroute from PC1 starts at the ISP router; and FW1 ignores pings to its outside address (`icmp deny any outside`).
column3: FW1 tiene tres interfaces con nombre: inside (nivel 100), dmz (50) y outside (0). La oficina y la DMZ salen a Internet con la dirección externa (`show xlate`, `show conn`); Home no puede iniciar nada hacia ellas, salvo hacia el servidor web, publicado como 203.0.113.10 con una regla estática y una regla de acceso (`show access-list` cuenta los aciertos). Desde Home, abre http://203.0.113.10 y haz ping a PC1 para ver la diferencia; `show logging` en FW1 explica por qué se descartó un paquete. La política global inspecciona ICMP, así que los pings de la oficina vuelven sin regla; FW1 no cuenta como salto, así que un traceroute desde PC1 empieza en el router del ISP; y FW1 no responde a pings a su dirección externa (`icmp deny any outside`).
